content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in El Paso

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your PMI Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review PMI's specific hour requirements based on your degree level, then gather evidence of your hands-on project work. Eligibility is the foundation; confirm it before enrolling to avoid delays in your application.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Bootcamp. Attend synchronous sessions led by active certified practitioners, covering the PMBOK Guide and exam domains. Live interaction allows you to ask questions in real time and move through the curriculum at a structured pace designed to prepare you for success.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application & Fee
steps_items.text: After finishing your contact hours, create your PMI account and formally apply for PMP eligibility review. Upload documentation of your education and project experience, then pay the PMI examination fee. Plan for review time; PMI will confirm your eligibility before you can schedule your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the PMP Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-prep resources—practice questions, study guides, and review sessions—to build confidence. Schedule your exam with Pearson VUE at a test center convenient to you in El Paso. Sit for the computer-based exam and apply the knowledge you've mastered in your bootcamp training.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: After passing, you'll earn your PMP credential valid for three years. To renew, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, conferences, volunteer project work, or published articles. Plan your PDU strategy early so renewal stays on track and your credential remains active throughout your career.
